cf.title: Proposal: Conflict log history table for Logical Replication

input.subject: Proposal: Conflict log history table for Logical Replication

verdict_reasoning: No objection to the goal or to demand survived, and a committer who knows logical replication takes part in the thread. The five surviving objections are all fixable level 2 design points. The two_phase lock handling (replication-ondisk-2, security-1) is still open in messages #744 to #746. The other three are recorded key text that depends on session settings (standards-compat-1), `alter subscription` dropping data (standards-compat-3), and the regular dump of rows and grants (standards-compat-2).

brief.title: Conflict log table for logical replication conflicts
brief.problem: Logical replication conflicts go only to the server log as plain text. Querying them, getting structured fields such as table, LSN or old and new data, and feeding them to monitoring or resolution scripts are all hard. The audience is subscriber administrators and external tools.
brief.proposed_design: A new subscription option, conflict_log_destination (log, table or all), makes the system create a table pg_conflict.pg_conflict_log_<subid>, owned by the subscription and dropped with it. The apply worker inserts one row per LOG-level conflict, with the replica identity key as JSON and local tuple metadata as json[]. ERROR-level conflicts still go only to the server log, and the table is never published.
user_visible_surface: Subscription option conflict_log_destination = 'log' | 'table' | 'all' for create subscription and alter subscription.

New schema pg_conflict with table pg_conflict_log_<subid>; columns include conflict_type, remote_xid, remote_commit_lsn, remote_commit_ts, apply_origin, replica_identity, replica_identity_full, local_conflicts, has_omitted_values.
Key values over 64kB stored as the marker {"omitted":true,"length":...}.
drop subscription and alter subscription to 'log' refused while prepared transactions exist, when two_phase is on.
pg_dump/pg_upgrade and psql \dRs changes, in separate later patches.
author_claims: Structured rows are easier to query and analyze than server log text.
A user table, as opposed to a catalog, allows user purging and later partitioning.
Omitting oversized values instead of truncating them keeps equality and join queries on the table correct.
Similar extension-managed tables exist in BDR and pgactive.
brief.thread_state: The thread is long, and a core group reviewed it at v93: Amit Kapila, shveta malik, Nisha Moond, vignesh C, Zhijie Hou, Peter Smith and Masahiko Sawada. Sawada's objection to erroring out the apply worker only for the conflict log table under two_phase is still open, and the visible discussion does not settle documentation versus detection.
unclear: The main patch has no retention or purge mechanism for rows, though one was discussed early.
The material does not show what the visible messages mean by "what is in master now", or which parts are committed.
The patches do not say how a reader learns which DateStyle, timezone or other output settings were used when a row was written.
A user can create a fake pg_gid_<subid>_* prepared transaction and so block drop subscription or make apply fail; the material proposes no fix.
Some apply-worker cases, such as binary mode or type differences between publisher and subscriber, can still fail with an error above 1GB; the patch only documents this.

prior_attempts.title: Detection and resolution of logical replication conflict
prior_attempts.reason: The visible messages do not show why. The patch set was still under review at v17 in October 2024, and the last message shown, from 2024-10-28, has no reply. Two items were still open at that point: clock-skew handling, and a race in which DirtySnapshot index scans miss rows and report update_missing or delete_missing instead of the origin_differs conflicts.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 added resolvers that choose an outcome per conflict type. This proposal only records conflicts the apply worker already detects and reports, and resolves nothing.

objections.title: Apply worker errors on conflict log table lock contention under two_phase
objections.failure_scenario: A two_phase subscriber with track_commit_timestamp on records update_origin_differs rows after initial sync, while other prepared transactions are pending. Autovacuum truncation of the conflict log table makes the lock unavailable, and the apply worker errors. With disable_on_error, the subscription is disabled again and again.
objections.argument: The prepared-transaction check does not test whether a prepared transaction actually holds the table lock, so it gives false positives (message #731). Message #744 says these conflicts are routine after table sync and that the special error path is no easier to understand than a stall. Messages #745 and #746 still weigh documentation against detection, and the AI-written lock-holder check in message #733 was not adopted.
objections.author_must_show: Which conditions lead the apply worker to raise this error when no prepared transaction holds a lock on the conflict log table, and how often do they occur in a two_phase deployment?

critic.reasoning: Message #731 describes the false positive, and #744 says the triggering conditions are common after table sync. Messages #745 and #746 still weigh documentation against detection, so the thread has not answered it.

objections.title: Any role can block drop subscription with a fake prepared transaction
objections.failure_scenario: An unprivileged user on a subscriber with max_prepared_transactions > 0 runs PREPARE TRANSACTION 'pg_gid_<subid>_1' on an empty transaction. For a two_phase subscription with a conflict log table, drop subscription and alter subscription to 'log' are then refused. The apply worker may also error out on its next lock wait. The administrator sees only an error about prepared transactions.
objections.argument: The new refusals and the apply-worker error depend on finding prepared transactions for the subscription, and message #731 says the GID check tests only the name format. Message #733 compares this to replication slot names. Message #744 answers that creating a slot needs the REPLICATION privilege, while any role can prepare a transaction. The thread does not settle the point, and no fix is proposed, so the patch adds a denial-of-service lever for unprivileged roles that did not exist before.
objections.author_must_show: How do the new prepared-transaction checks tell a GID created by the apply worker from one any role can create with the same name?

critic.reasoning: Message #731 states the check tests only the GID format, and #744 answers the slot-name comparison in #733. A superuser can find and roll back the fake transaction through pg_prepared_xacts, so the harm is bounded, but the proposal has no fix.

objections.title: Recorded key text depends on the apply worker's output settings
objections.failure_scenario: An administrator sets DateStyle = 'SQL, DMY' on the subscriber database, and the apply worker records the key 2 January as "02/01/2025". A monitoring job running with MDY casts replica_identity->>'k' back to timestamptz and gets 1 February. Nothing in the row says which settings were used, so the job matches the wrong row.
objections.argument: Message #651 and #661 show the ambiguity, and #674 confirms that IntervalStyle and extra_float_digits behave the same way, and #738 and #741 add timezone and lc_monetary. Message #699 drops the fix and chooses documentation, but the documentation tells readers to cast with "the same settings that the apply worker used". Message #709 notes that a reader cannot find those settings. libpqwalreceiver already forces these settings so that values are unambiguous, so a committer would likely ask why the conflict log table, whose docs recommend casting back, does not do the same.
objections.author_must_show: How does a reader cast a recorded key back to its original value when the apply worker's DateStyle at write time is not recorded anywhere?

critic.reasoning: The thread weighed this cost and chose documentation in #699 and #702. But #709 shows a row does not record the write-time settings, so a reader cannot follow the documented advice to cast with them.

objections.title: Changing a logging option silently drops the table and user objects
objections.failure_scenario: An operator runs alter subscription s set (conflict_log_destination = 'log') to reduce load. The command permanently deletes all recorded conflicts. It also drops views and functions that other roles built on the table, and the subscription owner needs no privilege on those objects. The operator sees only a NOTICE.
objections.argument: Message #654 shows that the drop uses DROP_CASCADE and PERFORM_DELETION_INTERNAL, so event triggers do not see the cascaded objects. It also points out that drop_subscription.sgml still says CASCADE and RESTRICT have no effect. The fix in message #690 makes DROP SUBSCRIPTION honour RESTRICT. Message #654 suggests an error for ALTER, but neither message shows that this was settled. No other ALTER ... SET of a storage parameter or option in Postgres destroys user data, so a committer would likely ask for an explicit verb or a RESTRICT-style error.
objections.author_must_show: Why should alter subscription ... set (conflict_log_destination = 'log') drop the table and its dependents without an error, when drop table refuses by default?

critic.reasoning: The docs warn that the data is deleted, and #658 and #659 agree to honor RESTRICT. The patch in #690 covers only DROP SUBSCRIPTION, and the visible v93 material does not show the ALTER case settled.

objections.title: OID-based table name breaks dump, restore and user queries
objections.failure_scenario: A user builds views and scripts on pg_conflict.pg_conflict_log_16390 and grants SELECT to a monitoring role. After a pg_dump and restore, or after the subscription is recreated, the table is pg_conflict_log_<new oid>, empty, and without the grants. The user finds out when the monitoring stops returning rows.
objections.argument: The user-facing name of the table is built from the subscription OID, which is not stable across dump and restore. Message #742 states that a regular dump emits neither the table definition nor its privileges, and the brief puts pg_dump and pg_upgrade support in separate later patches. Recorded conflict rows are not carried over by a logical dump at all. pg_toast_<oid> follows the same naming pattern, but users do not query TOAST tables or grant privileges on them.
objections.author_must_show: How does a user refer to a subscription's conflict log table by a stable name, and what does a logical dump and restore do with its rows and grants?

critic.reasoning: Message #742 confirms a regular dump does not carry grants on the conflict log table, and the table name changes with the subscription OID. v93-0002 covers the destination and binary upgrade, but not rows or grants in a regular dump.

refuted.title: Any user can block DROP SUBSCRIPTION with a fake pg_gid prepared transaction
refuted.failure_scenario: An unprivileged user runs PREPARE TRANSACTION 'pg_gid_<subid>_1' on the subscriber. DROP SUBSCRIPTION and ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SET (conflict_log_destination = 'log') are then refused, and with two_phase on, the apply worker errors whenever the conflict log table lock is contended. The administrator cannot see which session caused this.
refuted.argument: The new checks match prepared transactions by GID format only, and any role can create a prepared transaction (message #731). Message #733 compares this to reserved slot names, but message #744 notes that creating a slot needs REPLICATION while PREPARE TRANSACTION needs no privilege. The proposal adds no protection, and the brief lists this case as unresolved.
refuted.author_must_show: How does the check tell prepared transactions the apply worker created from user-created ones with the same GID pattern, so an unprivileged role cannot block subscription DDL?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1. Its claim that the administrator cannot find the cause is also weak, because pg_prepared_xacts shows the GID and its owner.

refuted.title: Stored replica_identity text depends on unrecorded apply worker settings
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA changes the database DateStyle from ISO, DMY to SQL, DMY, and later conflicts are stored as "02/01/2025". A resolution script reading under MDY casts replica_identity->>'k' to timestamptz and gets 1 February, not 2 January. It then matches or repairs the wrong row without any error.
refuted.argument: Message #651 showed the wrong result, and messages #672 and #674 confirmed the same for IntervalStyle and extra_float_digits. A fix was dropped in message #699 in favour of a documentation note that tells readers to cast using the settings the apply worker used. Message #709 points out that a row does not record those settings, so the stored value cannot be read back reliably once the settings have changed.
refuted.author_must_show: Given a single conflict log row written in the past, how does a reader recover the original key value without knowing the apply worker's DateStyle and IntervalStyle at write time?

refuted.title: Main patch lands before dump, upgrade and data carry-over are settled
refuted.failure_scenario: A user turns on conflict_log_destination = 'table', grants SELECT on the table to a monitoring role, and later restores from pg_dump. The restored subscription gets a new empty table named after a new subid, and both the grants and the recorded conflicts are gone. With pg_upgrade, the outcome depends on follow-up patches that are not yet committed.
refuted.argument: The brief places pg_dump and pg_upgrade support in separate later patches, while message #726 plans to commit the insertion patch first. Message #742 notes that a regular dump drops privileges on the conflict log table. Message #733 says carrying data across major versions is still under discussion.
refuted.author_must_show: What happens to existing conflict log table rows and privileges across pg_dump/restore and pg_upgrade if only the main patch is committed for this release?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. Committing the insertion patch before v93-0002 in the same series is the usual infrastructure-first order, and the material does not show a release shipping without it.

refuted.title: One conflict log table exposes key values from every replicated table
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator grants SELECT on pg_conflict.pg_conflict_log_<subid> to a monitoring role, as message #6 suggests. The role can then read replica identity values, for example email or account keys, from tables where it has no SELECT, no column privilege, or where row-level security hides the rows. Nobody is warned when the grant is made.
refuted.argument: Before the patch these values appeared only in the server log, which ordinary roles cannot read. The patch moves them into one relation with one ACL for all tables in the subscription. Column privileges and row-level security on the source tables do not apply to it. The material does not state the default ACL on the table or on the pg_conflict schema, and the documentation hunks do not warn that a grant on this table bypasses source-table privileges.
refuted.author_must_show: What is the default ACL on pg_conflict and its tables, and where do the docs warn that granting SELECT bypasses source-table column privileges and row-level security?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs an administrator to grant SELECT on the conflict log table, and a grant on any table exposes its contents. The material shows no default access for ordinary roles, so no exposure happens without that deliberate act.

refuted.title: Special lock handling for the conflict log table under two_phase
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator runs a subscription with two_phase on and track_commit_timestamp on. Autovacuum truncates the conflict log table while any pg_gid_<subid>_* prepared transaction exists. The apply worker raises an error, and with disable_on_error the subscription stays disabled until someone re-enables it.
refuted.argument: The design adds locking rules that apply only to this table: a conditional lock attempt, a scan of the prepared transactions by GID format, and lock_timeout set to deadlock_timeout plus 5s. Message #731 shows that the check gives false positives and that any user can create a matching GID. Message #744 notes that after the initial table sync these conflicts are common, and the question of why the table needs its own rules is still open in messages #745 and #746. Future changes to lock handling, autovacuum truncation or two_phase must keep this special path working, and no test fails loudly if they do not.
refuted.author_must_show: Why does the conflict log table need its own lock-wait rules, when documenting the existing PREPARE TRANSACTION hazard covers normal tables?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2. Its claim that no test covers the special path does not match #665 and #683, which add tests for the new error and the lock scenario.

refuted.title: Recorded key text depends on the apply worker's output settings
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator changes DateStyle for the subscriber database, and later conflicts store the key as '02/01/2025'. A monitoring query casts replica_identity->>'k' to timestamptz under a different DateStyle and matches the wrong row. Nothing in the conflict log table records which settings were used when the row was written.
refuted.argument: The list of settings that change the stored text grew in the thread from two to seven (messages #677, #672, #738, #741), and a fix that pinned these settings was dropped in favour of documentation (messages #699, #702). Message #709 notes that a reader cannot find out which settings applied to a past row. Any future setting that changes a type's output text will have to be added to this caveat, and nothing fails when that is missed. The table is meant for monitoring and resolution scripts (message #1), and those scripts depend on stable keys.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is storing the key text in the session-dependent format acceptable for tools that compare or cast these keys, when the walreceiver pins these settings for the same reason?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The v92 docs were also reworded to be generic, so the list of settings no longer needs an entry per setting.

refuted.title: Dump and upgrade support is in later, uncommitted patches
refuted.failure_scenario: A release ships the conflict log table, but the patch that preserves conflict_log_destination and the table is still pending. A user runs pg_upgrade or pg_dump and restore. The subscription returns with destination 'log', and the recorded conflict history is lost without any error.
refuted.argument: The insertion patch (v88/v93-0001) is about to be committed (message #726). The pg_dump/pg_upgrade patch is still under review as v93-0002 (messages #742, #747), and message #733 calls carry-over of the table data a later step. Message #742 also notes that a regular dump does not restore grants on the table. A new kind of user-visible object needs pg_dump coverage before or together with the feature, not in a later release.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the pg_dump and pg_upgrade patch be committed in the same release as the conflict log table, and what happens to existing rows and grants in a regular dump?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. The scenario assumes a release without the dump patch, but v93-0002 is under review in the same series and nothing shows it slipping to a later release.

refuted.title: Structured jsonlog output already covers part of the need
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator already ships `log_destination = 'jsonlog'` to a log pipeline. With this patch, the same conflicts also land in a per-subscription table with its own retention, and that table is deleted on `drop subscription`. Each copy then holds part of the conflict history, and its text form depends on the apply worker's DateStyle or bytea_output.
refuted.argument: Since Postgres 15, jsonlog emits each conflict message as a JSON object, and file_fdw or pg_read_file can query it with SQL. The real gap is that table, key values and origin sit inside the DETAIL text. A smaller change would add those as structured fields to the log entry, which is less code than the table this patch adds. Message #1 says text logs are hard to parse, but the proposal does not say why jsonlog plus structured fields would not be enough.
refuted.author_must_show: What would a user still be unable to do if conflict key, origin and xid were added as structured jsonlog fields instead of a new table?

critic.reasoning: The objection concedes that jsonlog today leaves table, key and origin inside the DETAIL text, so the existing alternative cannot do the job. The thread shows demand from many reviewers, and BDR and pgactive have such tables.

refuted.title: A conflict-report hook could let extensions own the table
refuted.failure_scenario: A user wants retention, partitioning, or the remote tuple, none of which the first version provides. Because the table is created and dropped by core, they wait for a later major release. Meanwhile core keeps the two_phase lock rules, the 1GB rendering limits and the pg_dump special cases.
refuted.argument: Message #4 notes that BDR and pgactive manage conflict tables as extension-owned tables, so the model already works outside core. A hook in ReportApplyConflict that passes the structured conflict data would let an extension choose its schema, formatting and retention. Message #8 gives the reason for a user table as user control over purging and partitioning, but this patch leaves both for later (messages #2, #660). The proposal does not say what core placement gives that a hook-based extension cannot have.
refuted.author_must_show: What does core placement provide that an extension using a hook in ReportApplyConflict could not, given that BDR and pgactive already manage such tables?

critic.reasoning: No such hook exists in the core apply worker today, and BDR and pgactive use their own apply code. The scenario is not a failure: the feature is opt-in, and the owner can purge rows from the user table.

refuted.title: Table omits the ERROR-level conflicts that resolution scripts most need
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator builds a monitoring or resolution script on pg_conflict_log_<subid>. An insert_exists or multiple_unique_conflicts conflict stops replication, but no row appears, so the script sees nothing. The administrator learns this only from the server log, which is the text the feature was meant to replace.
refuted.argument: Message #1 justifies the feature with monitoring and "custom resolution scripts". The v87 patches record only LOG-level conflicts, which are already applied or skipped, and send ERROR-level ones to the server log only. The docs now call the table an "audit trail" for after-the-fact review, which is a narrower goal than the one stated. The 1GB limit explains why ERROR-level conflicts are excluded, but no user in the thread says that LOG-level history alone meets their need.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users or tools need structured history of only applied or skipped conflicts, while conflicts that halt apply still have to be parsed from the server log?

critic.reasoning: The patch prose says ERROR-level conflicts abort the apply transaction, so they go to the server log and already stop replication visibly. LOG-level conflicts change or skip rows without stopping anything, and the docs state that this is the table's scope.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: A later patch in the series must carry the per-subscription conflict log table and its destination setting through pg_upgrade.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The apply worker inserts conflict rows and gets new lock and error rules under two_phase.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch adds the pg_conflict schema, system-created tables named by subscription OID, and a new pg_subscription field.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch adds the option conflict_log_destination to create subscription and alter subscription.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump must restore the destination setting, and a regular dump carries neither rows nor grants of the table (message #742).

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: A later patch changes the \dRs output.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The prepared-transaction checks match GIDs by name format, and the table drop cascades to objects owned by other roles.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds lock rules for one table, the 64kB and 1GB value limits, and pg_dump special cases.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Under two_phase, when does the apply worker raise the lock error although no prepared transaction holds a lock on the conflict log table, and how often does that occur?
How do the prepared-transaction checks tell a GID that the apply worker created from one that any role created with the same pg_gid_<subid>_ name?
How does a reader cast a recorded key back to its original value when the row does not record the apply worker's DateStyle or timezone?
Why does `alter subscription ... set (conflict_log_destination = 'log')` drop the table and its dependent objects without an error, when DROP SUBSCRIPTION now honours RESTRICT?
What does a regular pg_dump and restore do with the rows and grants of the conflict log table, and how do users purge old rows?

committability.owner_note: Amit Kapila, who works on logical replication, reviews the series and plans to commit the insertion patch (message #726). Masahiko Sawada also reviews, and his two_phase objection is open.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new schema with system-created user tables, the pg_dump and pg_upgrade special cases, and the two_phase lock rules in the apply worker. The table format and the option values become user-visible and are hard to change later.
committability.author_follow_up: The author has posted more than 90 versions since August 2025, and the entry was rebased through October 2026, so the author stays with the work.

priority.reason: Subscriber administrators who meet conflicts gain a queryable record, and BDR and pgactive have similar tables. The main patch is about 100 KiB in the apply worker and subscription commands, but a qualified committer is engaged and the open points are fixable.

provisional_note: The code was not read, and only 3 of 747 messages were visible directly. The lock handling under two_phase, the cascade drop path and the pg_dump patch need a check against the latest version.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Detection and resolution of logical replication conflict
precedents_retrieved.authors: Zhijie Hou (houzj), shveta malik (shvetam), Nisha Moond (nishamoond)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal adds conflict detection and resolution to the logical replication apply worker, with conflict types such as insert_exists, update_origin_differs, update_missing and delete_missing. Users pick a built-in resolver (for example apply_remote, keep_local, skip, error or last_update_wins) per conflict type, first as a global setting and later as a CONFLICT RESOLVER clause on CREATE SUBSCRIPTION.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The patch set was still under review at v17 in October 2024, and the last message shown, from 2024-10-28, has no reply. Two items were still open at that point: clock-skew handling, and a race in which DirtySnapshot index scans miss rows and report update_missing or delete_missing instead of the origin_differs conflicts.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow self-conflicting INSERT INTO .. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATEs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE accept a command whose own proposed rows conflict with each other, as DO NOTHING already does. Today such a command fails with "command cannot affect row a second time".
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Peter Geoghegan voted against it, and the CFM returned it citing those two votes. Andres Freund objected that the patch makes one command update a row it inserted, producing cmin == cmax and breaking heap visibility rules. The author then found visibility bugs in his own patch. Peter Geoghegan argued that updating the same row twice in one command is not desirable and asked who would want it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: To me it seems as if allowing the same command to update the same row more than once is just not desirable in general.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: add subscription TAP test option "vcregress subscriptioncheck" for MSVC builds
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a "subscriptioncheck" option to vcregress.pl so that MSVC builds can run the subscription TAP tests with one command, like "recoverycheck". Later the thread moved to a documentation patch that describes "vcregress taptest" for Windows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan objected to adding more special targets to vcregress.pl, because the generic taptest option already runs any TAP test set with "vcregress taptest src/test/subscription". The author agreed and switched to a documentation patch. Juan José Santamaría Flecha reviewed that patch and asked for a typo fix and new wording, and the visible messages show no revised version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I would actually prefer to reduce the number of special things in
vcregress.pl rather than add more.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: Petr Jelinek posted a WIP patch set for built-in logical replication, with publication and subscription catalogs and DDL, a logical replication protocol and output plugin, and apply workers started by a launcher. It also included a proof-of-concept initial data copy, and left out sequences, DDL replication, TRUNCATE, ACLs and full pg_dump support.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The CF manager returned the entry because the newest patch was three weeks old while review was still ongoing. Peter Eisentraut had posted detailed reviews of each patch, Steve Singer had reported bugs such as a crash in the apply worker after column changes on the subscriber, and no updated version followed. Review found no design objection that blocked the work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The newest patch is 3-week old, so marking this entry as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Row filtering for logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an optional WHERE clause to tables in CREATE PUBLICATION so that the logical replication output plugin sends only rows matching the filter to subscribers. Initial table synchronization was not covered by the filter in this version.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was waiting on the author for several months after reviewers reported bugs and open issues (restricting the filter expression to the current tuple and immutable functions, a reproducible bug in cascaded replication), and it no longer applied. It was returned with feedback for that reason, with an invitation to rebase and resubmit.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch has been waiting on author for a couple of months and does
not apply anymore, so I am marking as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: transaction statistics of logical replication subscription
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread first proposed counting failed transactions and their sizes in pg_stat_replication_slots, so that users could tell successful logical decoding from repeated failed attempts. By the last version, the patch instead added apply_commit_count and apply_rollback_count columns to pg_stat_subscription_stats.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila noted that pg_stat_database already shows committed and rolled-back transactions per database, so the new counters largely duplicate it, and he asked whether anyone saw value in them. Masahiko Sawada agreed that commit and rollback counts without transaction sizes no longer meet the original goal and have no concrete use case. The author then marked the entry Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But I’m concerned that adding only apply_commit_count
and apply_rollback_count ends up adding the duplicate statistics with
no concrete use cases.

precedents_retrieved.title: Warning for Datatype mismatch between subscriber table and publisher table for logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical replication emit a warning when a subscriber table column has a different data type from the matching publisher column. The goal is to show type mismatches early so users can debug replication problems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not revise the patch after review, and it had not passed CI since about mid March, so the CF entry was closed. Ashutosh Bapat had asked for the unrelated file renames to be removed. He also noted that the code maps columns by position, and that it compares type OIDs and names on the subscriber without using the remote type cache.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since this has not been fixed, and the patch has not passed CI since at least
mid March, I'll close this CF entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Allow ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING on a partitioned table."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Allow ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING on a partitioned table."
Reverted commit(s): Allow ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING on a partitioned table.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 8355a011a0124bdf7ccbada206a967d427039553, which
turns out to have been a misguided effort.  We can't really support
this in a partitioning hierarchy after all for exactly the reasons
stated in the documentation removed by that commit.  It's still
possible to use ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING (or for that matter ON
CONFLICT .. DO UPDATE) on individual partitions if desired, but
but to allow this on a partitioned table implies that we have some
way of evaluating uniqueness across the whole partitioning
hierarchy, which is false.

Shinoda Noriyoshi noticed that the old code was crashing (which we
could fix, though not in a nice way) and Amit Langote realized
that this was indicative of a fundamental problem with the commit
being reverted here.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent proposed a conflict log table, and P1's open items (clock skew, the DirtySnapshot race) concern detection and resolution, which the current server log shares. Message #8 points to related threads on a COPY error table, and the material does not report a rejection reason for them.
Objections were found from the standards and compatibility angle.
The table is never published and its inserts use HEAP_INSERT_NO_LOGICAL. It replicates physically as an ordinary heap, so I see no standby or WAL record format issue.
The cross-owner cascade drop raised in message #654 is left out because option b was agreed in messages #658 and #659, and a patch for it was posted in message #690.

Hot-path cost falls only on subscriptions that set conflict_log_destination to table or all, and Amit Kapila, the committer in this area, is engaged and plans to commit. For these reasons no objection is raised on performance or ownership.
Two objections from the existing-alternative angle. Both are fixable, not fatal.

The thread shows real demand for structured conflict records: BDR and pgactive ship similar tables, several companies review the patch, and outside testers report results in messages #556, #569 and #620. The objection above concerns which conflicts the table covers, not whether anyone wants it.
